summary: A very short note from 1971 that reserves one link number, 191, on the early ARPANET for network measurement work. The number was meant to be the highest unassigned link, but an earlier calculation of 223 had been wrong. Anyone wanting to use the link was asked to clear it first with the Liaison Officer at the Network Measurement Center.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 104 corrects the link number reserved for measurement work. It says the assigned link is 191, not 223, and asks users to clear its use with the Network Measurement Center's Liaison Officer.

subtitle: Reserves link 191 for network measurement use.

tldr.problem: A Network Working Group meeting agreed to reserve a link for network measurements, but the number initially calculated for it was incorrect.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 104 corrects the number from 223 to 191 and assigns link 191 for measurement use.
tldr.outcome: Use of link 191 should be cleared with the Liaison Officer at the Network Measurement Center.

today: RFC 104 is an early link assignment note. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that updates or replaces it.

sections.title: A Link Reserved for Measurements
sections.content: At a Network meeting at the University of Illinois, participants agreed to reserve a link for measurements. The selected link was intended to be the highest unassigned link.
sections.plainLanguage: The note records an agreement to set aside one unassigned link for measurement use.

sections.title: Correcting the Link Number
sections.content: The earlier calculation identified the highest unassigned link as 223. RFC 104 says that calculation was incorrect and gives the correct number as 191.
sections.plainLanguage: The correct link number is 191. The earlier value, 223, was a miscalculation.

sections.title: Clearing Use of Link 191
sections.content: RFC 104 assigns link 191 for measurement use. It says that use of the link should be cleared with the Liaison Officer at the Network Measurement Center.
sections.plainLanguage: Anyone planning to use link 191 should first clear it with the Network Measurement Center's Liaison Officer.
